title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
authors: DeepSeek-AI (core contributors include Daya Guo, Dejian Yang, Haowei Zhang, Junxiao Song, Peiyi Wang, Qihao Zhu, Runxin Xu, Ruoyu Zhang, Shirong Ma, Xiao Bi and Zhihong Shao; corresponding author of the Nature version Yu Wu)
venue: arXiv report (January 2025), then Nature 645, 633 to 638 (17 September 2025); arXiv v2 (4 January 2026) carries the Nature text and its supplementary information
date: arXiv v1 22 January 2025; submitted to Nature 14 February 2025, accepted 17 July 2025, published 17 September 2025; arXiv v2 4 January 2026
run_label: train a tiny R1-Zero in your browser

code.title: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
code.note: the official repository: the README (models, evaluation settings, usage recommendations), the January paper as a PDF and the MIT licence; weights on Hugging Face (R1, R1-Zero, six distilled models). No training code, no RL code and no data, although the Nature paper's data statement points here. About 20 minutes for the README and the entry path

takeaway: Pure GRPO RL with rule-based verifiable rewards on V3-Base makes reasoning (reflection, "aha moment", long CoT) emerge without SFT; a cold-start SFT, reasoning RL, rejection-sampling SFT, all-scenario RL pipeline fixes R1-Zero's readability and language mixing to match o1, and 800k R1 samples distill reasoning into 1.5B-70B models by SFT alone.
verdict: Believe the central result: outcome-only RL on a strong base model produced long, self-checking reasoning, and many groups reproduced the effect within months. Treat the benchmark margins (R1 against o1, stage against stage) as single runs on small test sets, the cost as GPU rental for the RL alone, and the reflective behaviours as counted words rather than measured reasoning.

headline.k: DeepSeek-R1-Zero, AIME 2024 pass@1, from the base model with no supervised data: rule rewards only
headline.d: 86.7% with a 16-sample majority vote; the human average is 37.8% (decoded from Figure 1)

headline.k: GPU rental for R1-Zero, the SFT data and R1 together: 147K H800 hours at $2
headline.d: on top of V3-Base's reported 2,788K hours; 5.3% of it (derived)

headline.k: Qwen2.5-32B fine-tuned on R1's 800K samples, against the same base after 10K+ steps of R1-Zero-style RL
headline.d: distillation wins on all five benchmarks, by 2.7 to 25.6 points

kb.n: introduced GRPO; its page trains PPO, GRPO and the other methods side by side and traces the objective to DAPO and Dr. GRPO. R1 is GRPO scaled up with verifiable instead of learned rewards.
the 671B MoE base both R1-Zero and R1 start from; its SFT data supplies the 200K non-reasoning samples, and its bill is the $5.576M the $294K sits on.
the SFT-then-RLHF paradigm this paper partly inverts (RL before any reasoning SFT, rules before reward models); its page runs a toy PPO pipeline.
the offline alternative for preference alignment; R1's fourth stage shows where online RL with learned preference rewards is still used, and how quickly it is hacked.
a descendant family trained with an R1-style long chain-of-thought RL pipeline; Qwen2.5 models are also the distillation students here.
Llama-3.1-8B and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct are two of the six distillation students.

topics.n: the GRPO group calculator (how often a group gives no signal), R1's place in the history of test-time compute, serial against parallel thinking.
the R1 recipe as a flow with the distilled students, R1's inference system and prices, and where R1 sits in DeepSeek's line from V2 to V4.
RLVR, GRPO and RL for LLMs.
